 WHO Director-General's remarks at the visit to the Global Training Hub for Biomanufacturing – 20 October 2026
 WHO Director-General's remarks at the visit to the Global Training Hub for Biomanufacturing – 20 October 2026
 26 October 2026 
 Remarks 
 Incheon, Republic of Korea 
 Reading time: 
 Honourable Minister Dr Jeong Eun Kyeong, 
 Distinguished guests, dear colleagues and friends,
 It is a great pleasure for me to visit the Global Bio Campus as the first stop on my first visit to the Republic of Korea.
 Thank you for such a warm welcome.
 The COVID-19 pandemic exposed many gaps in global health security.
 One of them was the stark global inequity in access to life-saving vaccines and other medical products.
 Manufacturing of these products is concentrated in too few countries, creating a dangerous dependency.
 Strengthening local and regional production is therefore essential.
 That’s why WHO established the Global Training Hub for Biomanufacturing here in the Republic of Korea.
 When we were considering where to locate the Hub, many countries were interested in hosting it, but one of the main reasons we decided to base it here was the strong commitment of the government.
 We were confident that it would be a success, and that’s what we’re seeing.
 Within just months of designation, the Hub launched its first official training program.
 Since then, the Hub has trained more than 4000 participants from more than 50 low- and middle-income countries, gaining vital hands-on skills.
 I am confident that these trainees will make valuable contributions in their home countries, improving manufacturing processes and strengthening local production capacities.
 I would like to express my heartfelt gratitude to the Korean Government for its substantial investment of US$ 30 million.
 I also thank everyone who has made this possible, including staff from the Ministry of Health and Welfare and WHO.
 But we’re only just beginning.
 WHO remains fully committed to collaborating closely with Korea so that the Hub continues to thrive.
 By strengthening our alignment with WHO Regional Training Centres, we will build a safer, more equitable world where no one is left behind in access to essential medical products.
 Thank you once again to the Government of the Republic of Korea, Incheon Metropolitan City, Yonsei University, and all our partners for your commitment to this vital mission.
 Thank you very much.
 Kam-sa-ham-nida.
